key_insight: Graph neural networks are now a cross-domain default for relational data, but their benefit depends on whether graph structure justifies the added compute and complexity.
engineering_relevance: The paper gives practitioners a domain-by-domain guide to choosing graph constructions and architectures while highlighting where GNNs are likely to fail under heterophily, scale, or temporal dynamics.
method: Unifies spectral and spatial GNN formulations under shared principles.
Connects model expressiveness to the Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy.
Reviews 12 application areas and maps graph-design choices to dominant architecture families.
evidence_signal: The survey compares reported gains across domains against baseline quality, split choice, and deployment realism, while emphasizing recurring failure modes such as heterophily and temporal difficulty.
watch_item: Public leaderboard gains can be misleading: weak baselines, favorable splits, and distribution shift may hide poor real-world robustness.
paper_title: Graph Neural Networks Applications Across Domains: All Insights You Need
